- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 66.97 or 68.02), then underestimates the subsequent correction.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too much upward bias when prices are trending down.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle to late horizon.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum — fails to account for volatility clustering or sudden policy-driven corrections.
- Tends to smooth out sharp drops in history, underestimating the depth of corrections.
- Overestimates the persistence of recent highs — fails to recognize that prices often revert to 65–67 range after 68+ peaks.
- Model exhibits “peak chasing” behavior — forecasts peak prices too high and then fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
